concepts.def: A process such as sawing, drilling, turning or milling that shapes a material by cutting away unwanted waste.
Reshaping a material without removing any waste, for example bending sheet metal, vacuum forming plastic or press forming, often after heating.
Shaping liquid or softened material inside a mould, as in injection moulding or casting, well suited to making many identical parts.
Joining methods such as welding, brazing and adhesives that cannot be undone without damaging the parts being joined.
Fastenings such as screws, nuts and bolts that hold parts together securely but still allow disassembly for maintenance or repair.
A treatment such as painting, varnishing, plating or polishing applied to a material to protect it and improve its appearance.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Manufacturing Processes & Techniques — a core area of GCSE Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Manufacturing Processes & Techniques brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Manufacturing Processes & Techniques.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a wasting (material removal) process?
options: Drilling
Vacuum forming
Injection moulding
Press forming

mcqs.q: Vacuum forming is most suitable for shaping which material?
options: Solid steel bar
Thermoplastic sheet
Hardwood plank
Thermosetting plastic powder
Welding
Adhesive bonding
Machine screws with nuts
Brazing

mcqs.q: Why is injection moulding suited to high-volume production?
options: The mould is very cheap to make
No surface finish is ever needed
Each product is unique and handmade
After the high initial mould cost, each part is produced quickly, cheaply and consistently

mcqs.q: What is the difference between vacuum forming and injection moulding?
options: Vacuum forming is only used for shaping metals.
They are the same process carried out at different temperatures.
Yes - sanding is a type of joining process.
Vacuum forming sucks a heated thermoplastic sheet down over a mould; injection moulding forces molten plastic into a closed mould under pressure.
No - sanding removes material as dust, so it is a wasting/finishing process; forming reshapes material without removing any waste.
Yes - any process that changes the shape of a material is forming.
Yes - sanding is a type of joining process.
Yes - rivets are a type of adhesive.

mcqs.q: Are pop rivets a temporary joining method?
options: Yes - any mechanical fastener without glue counts as temporary.
Vacuum forming is only used for shaping metals.
Yes - rivets are a type of adhesive.
No - rivets are permanent; they must be drilled out and destroyed to separate the parts.

sequence.def: 3D printing starts with a digital design

sequence.term: Model exported as an STL file
sequence.def: Geometry is converted to a printable mesh
Software turns the mesh into G-code layer paths
Material is deposited from the bottom upwards
Temporary structures are broken or dissolved away
Sanding or sealing completes the part
